business_model: Home health, hospice and personal-care services for mostly elderly patients; revenue comes from Medicare/Medicaid and managed-care payers, with growth partly from acquisitions.
key_reason: Revenue grew from $1.06B (2023) to $1.42B (2025), about 16% CAGR.
next_review_trigger: Valuation is fair, not cheap. Re-evaluate below ~18x earnings or if organic growth stays >8%.

business_model: Amentum provides engineering, mission support, nuclear and intelligence services mainly to U.S. and allied governments; contract mix is cost-plus and fixed-price.
next_review_trigger: Cheap on FCF but contract/accounting quality needs more work; watch, not buy.

company: Boot Barn Holdings, Inc. Common Stock
business_model: Boot Barn sells western, work and outdoor footwear/apparel through stores and e-commerce; growth comes from new stores and same-store sales.
key_reason: Revenue rose from $1.67B to $2.25B with positive comps.
next_review_trigger: ~18x earnings is fair for a good retailer but not a margin of safety; wait for a better price or comp proof.

company: Church & Dwight Company, Inc. Common Stock
business_model: Church & Dwight sells household and personal-care brands (Arm & Hammer, Trojan, OxiClean, vitamins) through mass retail and e-commerce.
key_reason: Steady revenue and strong brands; FCF $1.09B.
next_review_trigger: High-quality but expensive. Revisit below ~25x earnings with mid-single-digit organic growth.

business_model: Collegium markets abuse-deterrent prescription pain products (Xtampza ER, Belbuca) and receives royalties; earnings depend on payer access and product mix.
key_reason: FCF $328M on $781M revenue; cash generation strong.
next_review_trigger: Optically cheap but litigation tail risk prevents a CONTINUE; position sizing would be critical.

business_model: CorMedix commercializes DefenCath, an antimicrobial catheter-lock solution for dialysis patients; revenue depends on hospital/outpatient reimbursement and contracts.
key_reason: Q3 2026 revenue fell to $54.5M and net loss was -$14.7M; reimbursement/contract concentration; FY2025 earnings quality uncertain.
next_review_trigger: Trailing P/E is not meaningful given the quarterly loss; the apparent cheapness is a value trap until revenue stabilizes.

business_model: D.R. Horton is the largest U.S. homebuilder; revenue comes from home closings, with mortgage/financial services and lot sales.
key_reason: Scale and low-cost land strategy; FCF $3.35B.
next_review_trigger: Cyclically cheap but earnings are near a peak; wait for order stabilization or a deeper discount.

business_model: DoubleVerify provides independent ad verification, measurement and fraud detection software to advertisers and platforms.
next_review_trigger: Quality franchise but expensive for high-single-digit growth; wait for <25x earnings or reacceleration.

business_model: EPAM provides software engineering and product-development services, primarily to North American and European enterprises; revenue is project/headcount based.
next_review_trigger: Reasonable price for a high-quality franchise, but growth visibility is poor; watch for a return to double-digit growth.

business_model: Flexsteel designs and sells residential and hospitality furniture, mainly through wholesale channels; results are tied to housing and discretionary spending.
key_reason: Revenue and margins improved through FY2026; FCF $47.6M.
next_review_trigger: Cheap but low-quality cyclical; only for a basket/asset-value approach, not a core candidate.

business_model: Genpact runs business-process outsourcing and digital operations for large enterprises; revenue is recurring, contract-based and often multi-year.
next_review_trigger: Cheap cash-generative services business; a 10% FCF yield supports research. Re-evaluate if organic growth turns negative.

company: Grid Dynamics Holdings, Inc. - Class A Common Stock
business_model: Grid Dynamics provides digital-engineering and platform services, largely to U.S. retail/tech clients with delivery in Eastern Europe.
key_reason: P/E ~117 and EV/EBITDA ~47 with ~2.3% net margin; valuation disconnected from profitability.
next_review_trigger: Growth is real but the multiple is disconnected from profitability; eliminate at current price.

company: Global Ship Lease Inc New Class A Common Shares
business_model: Global Ship Lease owns and charters containerships under fixed-rate time charters; revenue depends on charter rates and fleet utilization.
key_reason: P/E ~3.5 and FCF yield ~36%, deeply cyclical value.
next_review_trigger: Statistically cheap but peak-cycle earnings; only for a cyclical/value specialist, not a core compounder.

company: Huntington Ingalls Industries, Inc. Common Stock
business_model: Huntington Ingalls builds nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and submarines for the U.S. Navy; revenue is long-cycle, cost-plus/incentive government contracting.
next_review_trigger: Fair value for a strategic asset; watch execution rather than pay a premium.

business_model: Interparfums develops and distributes fragrances under licensed brands (e.g., Coach, Guess, Jimmy Choo) and owns some brands; revenue is wholesale/retail sell-in.
next_review_trigger: Good business at a fair price; wait for a larger discount or evidence of mid-single-digit organic growth.

business_model: Stride provides online K-12 education, career learning and school services, largely funded by public/charter school programs and tuition.
next_review_trigger: Cheap, cash-generative and growing; research further, but regulatory risk caps position size.

business_model: Limbach provides mechanical, electrical and plumbing services and building-systems maintenance, with growing data-center work.
next_review_trigger: Fair price for a niche contractor; need more evidence on recurring maintenance mix.

company: El Pollo Loco Holdings, Inc. - Common Stock
business_model: El Pollo Loco operates and franchises fast-casual chicken restaurants, mainly in the U.S. Southwest; revenue comes from company restaurants and franchise royalties.
next_review_trigger: Neither cheap nor high-growth; watch only if unit economics improve.

company: NerdWallet, Inc. - Class A Common Stock
business_model: NerdWallet operates a personal-finance marketplace, earning performance-based fees when users apply for credit cards, loans, insurance and deposits.
next_review_trigger: Cheap optionality but traffic/concentration risk; mark as watch with data caveat.

business_model: OneSpan provides digital identity, authentication and e-signature software to banks and enterprises.
key_reason: Revenue flat at ~$243M; FY2024-25 net income boosted by non-operating items.
next_review_trigger: Flat revenue plus non-recurring earnings; eliminate unless ARR reaccelerates.

business_model: Progyny manages fertility and family-building benefits for large employers, earning fees from plan sponsors and utilization.
next_review_trigger: Good niche franchise but expensive; wait for <30x earnings and client diversification.

business_model: PulteGroup is a U.S. homebuilder with a focus on entry-level and move-up homes; revenue comes from closings and mortgage operations.
next_review_trigger: Cheap on book/earnings but cycle risk; wait for order stabilization.

business_model: PPG makes paints, coatings and specialty materials for industrial, automotive, aerospace and architectural customers.
next_review_trigger: Fair value for a quality cyclical; not cheap enough for a CONTINUE.

business_model: PROG Holdings offers lease-to-own and point-of-sale financing, mainly through retail partners; earnings depend on consumer credit and partner volumes.
next_review_trigger: Cheap on FCF but credit-cycle risk; watch, not core.

business_model: QuinStreet is a performance-marketing company focused on insurance, education and home services; revenue is media spend from clients.
next_review_trigger: Cheap but low-quality/cyclical; watch for margin durability.

company: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. - Common Stock
business_model: Reynolds Consumer Products sells Reynolds Wrap, Hefty, Presto and store-brand household products through mass retail.
next_review_trigger: Fair value for a staple; no margin of safety.

company: Sprouts Farmers Market, Inc. - Common Stock
business_model: Sprouts Farmers Market operates specialty grocery stores focused on fresh, natural and organic products; revenue comes from store sales.
next_review_trigger: Cheap enough to research further; re-evaluate if comps turn negative or FCF falls below $300M.

business_model: TransMedics sells organ-care systems and transplant services (lung, heart, liver), earning from perfusion devices and service fees.
key_reason: Revenue grew from $242M to $605M; FY2025 net income $190M.
next_review_trigger: High-quality growth but not cheap; research further only with a plan to buy on growth proof or a 25-30% drawdown.

business_model: Urban Outfitters operates Anthropologie, Urban Outfitters, Free People and Nuuly; revenue is store and e-commerce apparel/home.
next_review_trigger: Cheap enough to watch; need consistent comps before a CONTINUE.

business_model: WD-40 sells maintenance products, lubricants and specialty chemicals under WD-40, 3-IN-ONE and other brands worldwide.
key_reason: High gross margins and brand loyalty; FCF $98M.
next_review_trigger: Excellent business, expensive stock; wait for a 20-25% drawdown.
